# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
periods = ['P%02d'%i for i in range(1,10)]
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands])

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1  # 6 blocks
# block i: matching months i..i+m-1, forward month i+m
M = np.array([Y[:, i:i+m].ravel() for i in range(nb)])          # blocks x (bands*m)
F = np.array([Y[:, i+m].ravel() for i in range(nb)])            # forward month values
target = Y[:, 9-m:].ravel()                                      # matching window P07-P09

def fit(idx):
    A = M[list(idx)].T
    w, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, target, rcond=None)
    w = np.clip(w, 0, None); w = w/w.sum()
    err = np.mean((M[list(idx)].T@w - target)**2)

idx, w, err = best
pred = F[list(idx)].T @ w
print("kept blocks:", idx, "weights:", np.round(w,3), "match MSE: %.4f"%err)

Y = np.array([T[b] for b in bands])  # bands x 9

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1  # 6 blocks
# block i: matching months i..i+m-1, forward month i+m
M = np.array([Y[:, i:i+m] for i in range(nb)])  # blocks x bands x m
F = np.array([Y[:, i+m] for i in range(nb)])    # blocks x bands
target = Y[:, -m:]                              # bands x m (P07-P09)

def fit(idx):
    A = M[list(idx)].reshape(len(idx), -1).T   # (bands*m) x k
    b = target.reshape(-1)
    # nonneg least squares with sum-to-1 via scipy
    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    # augment for sum=1 penalty
    lam = 1e3
    A2 = np.vstack([A, lam*np.ones((1, A.shape[1]))])
    b2 = np.concatenate([b, [lam]])
    w, _ = nnls(A2, b2)
    s = w.sum()
    if s <= 0: return None, np.inf
    w = w/s
    err = np.mean((A @ w - b)**2)
    return w, err

best = (None, np.inf, None)
for k in range(1, nb+1):
    for idx in itertools.combinations(range(nb), k):
        w, err = fit(idx)
        if w is not None and err < best[1]:

pred = np.einsum('i,ij->j', w, F[list(idx)])

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

from scipy.optimize import nnls

t = Y[:, -m:].ravel()  # matching window P07-P09

best = (np.inf, None, None)
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for S in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        Ms = M[:, S]
        w, _ = nnls(Ms, t)
        if w.sum() < 1e-12: continue
        w = w / w.sum()
        err = np.mean((Ms @ w - t)**2)

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Implement and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction; every setting and every choice in it
is yours, made inside your program.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band. The same data is in
   `data.csv` in this directory: one row per band per month, columns `band`, `period_id`
   (P01–P09 in time order), `month` (YYYY-MM), `mean_value`.
2. Read `references/method.md`. Decide how to build the blocks, what to match, how to fit
   and constrain the weights, how to select blocks, and how to form the prediction.
3. Write `predict.py`. It reads `data.csv` and prints one line per band, `BAND VALUE`, the
   predicted mean value for the next month. numpy, scipy and pandas are available; nothing
   outside this directory is, and there is no network.
4. Run `python predict.py`. Fix what fails; run again. Every run is recorded.
5. Finish by writing `answer.json`:
   ```json
   {"prediction": {"<band>": <value>, ...}, "rationale": "<what the program does and why>"}

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).

forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in

Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, itertools, json

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df['band'].unique())
periods = [f'P{i:02d}' for i in range(1,10)]
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands]) # bands x 9

t = np.arange(9)
# preparation: remove annual sine/cosine after detrending with low-order (linear) trend
X = np.zeros((9,0))
prep = np.zeros_like(Y)
for i in range(len(bands)):
    y = Y[i]
    # design: trend, sin, cos (annual cycle ~ 12 months)
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(9), t, np.sin(2*np.pi*t/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*t/12)])
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(D, y, rcond=None)
    r = y - D@beta
    # local-linear Gaussian kernel smoothing, bandwidth h=1.5
    h = 1.5
    sm = np.zeros(9)
    for k in range(9):
        w = np.exp(-0.5*((t-k)/h)**2)
        Dk = np.column_stack([np.ones(9), t-k])
        W = np.diag(w)
        b = np.linalg.solve(Dk.T@W@Dk + 1e-8*np.eye(2), Dk.T@W@r)
        sm[k] = b[0]
    sm = sm - sm.mean()
    sd = sm.std()
    prep[i] = sm/sd if sd>1e-9 else sm

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9-m-n+1
blocks = [list(range(s, s+m)) for s in range(nb)]
forwards = [s+m for s in range(nb)]  # index of first forward month
match_win = list(range(9-m, 9))

M = np.array([[prep[i][j] for j in blk] for blk in blocks])  # blocks x m (per band stacked)
# build target vector: bands stacked
def block_vec(bi):
    return np.concatenate([prep[i][blocks[bi]] for i in range(len(bands))])
target = np.concatenate([prep[i][match_win] for i in range(len(bands))])
B = np.array([block_vec(b) for b in range(nb)])

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for sub in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        A = B[list(sub)].T
        w, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, target, rcond=None)
        w = np.clip(w, 0, None)  # nonnegative
        w = w/w.sum() if w.sum()>0 else w
        err = np.mean((B[list(sub)].T@w - target)**2)
        if best is None or err < best[0]-1e-12:
            best = (err, sub, w)
err, sub, w = best
print("kept blocks:", sub, "weights:", np.round(w,3), "match MSE:", err)

# prediction: weighted combination of first forward month, observed values
pred_obs = np.zeros(len(bands))
for k, bi in enumerate(sub):
    pred_obs += w[k]*Y[:, forwards[bi]]

# also prepared-space prediction with inverse transform, average with observed-space
# prepared-space: weighted combo of prepared forward values, then undo standardization,
# add back seasonal term for target month index t=9
pred_prep = np.zeros(len(bands))
for k, bi in enumerate(sub):
    pred_prep += w[k]*prep[:, forwards[bi]]
for i in range(len(bands)):
    y = Y[i]
    D = np.column_stack([np.ones(9), t, np.sin(2*np.pi*t/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*t/12)])
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(D, y, rcond=None)
    r = y - D@beta
    sm = r  # unsmoothed residual for scale/mean recovery approx
    mu, sd = sm.mean(), sm.std()
    D10 = np.array([1, 9, np.sin(2*np.pi*9/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*9/12)])
    pred_prep[i] = (pred_prep[i]*sd + mu) + D10@beta

pred = 0.5*pred_obs + 0.5*pred_prep
out = {b: round(float(v),4) for b,v in zip(bands, pred)}
for b,v in out.items(): print(b, v)
json.dump({"prediction": out, "rationale": "Synthetic historical control: bands prepared (annual sin/cos removed after linear trend, Gaussian local-linear smoothing h=1.5, standardized), m=3 matching window (P07-P09), n=1 forward month, 6 overlapping blocks, exhaustive nonnegative least-squares weight search over all subsets, prediction = weighted combination of forward months in observed space blended 50/50 with prepared-space prediction (seasonal term added back)."}, open('answer.json','w'), indent=1)
EOF
python predict.py

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
periods = [f'P{i:02d}' for i in range(1,10)]

nb = 9 - m - n + 1  # 6 blocks

    A = M[:, cols]
    w, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, t, rcond=None)

    if w.sum() <= 0: w = np.ones(len(cols))/len(cols)

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):

        if best is None or err < best[0]:

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

d = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
bands = sorted(d.band.unique())
w = d.pivot(index="period_id", columns="band", values="mean_value").sort_index()
Y = w[bands].values  # 9 x 3, P01..P09

# preparation: per band, standardize (mean0/sd1) over P01-P09
Z = (Y - Y.mean(0)) / Y.std(0)

m, n = 3, 1                       # matching length, forward length
nb = 9 - m - n + 1                # number of blocks = 6
M = np.stack([Z[i:i+m] for i in range(nb)])   # blocks' matching parts (nb, m, B)
F = np.stack([Y[i+m:i+m+n] for i in range(nb)])  # forward parts, observed (nb, n, B)
target = Z[9-m:]                  # matching window = most recent m months

def fit(idx):
    A = M[list(idx)].reshape(len(idx), -1).T   # (m*B, k)
    b = target.reshape(-1)

    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    wt, _ = nnls(A, b)
    err = np.mean((A @ wt - b) ** 2)
    return wt, err

        if best is None or err < best[1]:

Weights are nonnegative least squares fits of block matching parts to the most recent 3 months, jointly over all bands; exhaustive subset selection picks the lowest matching-MSE set. from scipy.optimize import minimize

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==f"P{i:02d}")].mean_value.iloc[0]
               for i in range(1,10)] for b in bands])

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1
M = np.column_stack([Y[:, i:i+m].T.flatten() for i in range(nb)])
target = Y[:, 9-m:].T.flatten()

def fit(idxs):
    A = M[:, list(idxs)]
    k = len(idxs)
    res = minimize(lambda w: np.mean((A@w - target)**2), np.ones(k)/k,
                   method='SLSQP', bounds=[(0,1)]*k,
                   constraints=[{'type':'eq','fun':lambda w: w.sum()-1}],
                   options={'maxiter':500,'ftol':1e-12})
    return res.fun, res.x

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for sub in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        err, w = fit(sub)
        if best is None or err < best[0]:
            best = (err, sub, w)

err, sub, w = best
print("kept blocks:", sub, "weights:", np.round(w,4), "match MSE:", round(err,5))
pred = np.zeros(len(bands))
for k, i in enumerate(sub):
    pred += w[k]*Y[:, i+m]
for b, v in zip(bands, pred):
    print(b, round(float(v), 4))

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, itertools

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
periods = [f'P{i:02d}' for i in range(1,10)]
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0] for p in periods] for b in bands])  # 3x9

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1  # 6 blocks
blocks = [np.arange(s, s+m) for s in range(nb)]
fwd = [s+m for s in range(nb)]
target = np.arange(9-m, 9)  # P07-P09

# standardize each band (prepared space, no seasonal removal needed for short series)
mu = Y.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True); sd = Y.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)
Z = (Y - mu)/sd

W = np.hstack([Z[:, b] for b in blocks])  # 3 x (6*3)
t = Z[:, target].flatten()

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for sub in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        cols = [c for s in sub for c in range(s*3, s*3+3)]
        A = W[:, cols]
        w, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, t, rcond=None)
        if (w < -1e-9).any(): continue
        w = np.clip(w, 0, None)
        if w.sum() <= 0: continue
        w = w/w.sum()
        err = np.mean((A @ w - t)**2)
        if best is None or err < best[0]:
            best = (err, sub, w)
err, sub, w = best
print('kept blocks:', [periods[s] for s in sub], 'err', err, 'w', w)

# prediction: weighted combination of forward months (first forward month), in observed space
# weights per block = sum of its column weights
wblock = np.array([w[i*3:(i+1)*3].sum() for i in range(len(sub))])
wblock = wblock/wblock.sum()
pred = {b: float(np.dot(wblock, Y[[bands.index(b)][0], [fwd[s] for s in sub]])) for b in bands}
for b, v in pred.items():
    print(b, round(v, 4))
import json
json.dump({'prediction': pred, 'rationale': 'Synthetic historical control: blocks of m=3 consecutive months with n=1 forward month from P01-P09; matching window is P07-P09. Bands standardized and stacked; nonnegative least-squares weights fitted jointly over all bands; exhaustive subset selection by matching MSE. Prediction is the weighted combination of the kept blocks first forward months, back in observed space.'}, open('answer.json','w'), indent=2)
EOF
python predict.py
```

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1  # 6 blocks

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import numpy as np, pandas as pd

d = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
w = d.pivot(index="period_id", columns="band", values="mean_value").sort_index()
bands = list(w.columns)
X = w.values  # 9 x 8, P01..P09
T = 9
t = np.arange(1, T + 1)

# --- preparation per band: remove annual sin/cos (after partialling out linear trend), smooth, standardize
def gaussian_smooth(y, bw=1.5):
    ys = np.empty_like(y)
    for i in range(len(y)):
        k = np.exp(-0.5 * ((t - t[i]) / bw) ** 2)
        # local-linear weights
        u = (t - t[i]) / bw
        s0, s1, s2 = k.sum(), (k * u).sum(), (k * u * u).sum()
        a = np.maximum(s2 - s1**2 / s0, 1e-12)
        wts = k * (1 + (u * (0 - s1 / s0)))  # local-linear hat for x=0
        ys[i] = (wts * y).sum() / wts.sum()
    return ys

prep = np.zeros_like(X)
params = {}
for j, b in enumerate(bands):
    y = X[:, j]
    # trend
    A = np.vstack([np.ones(T), t]).T
    beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, y, rcond=None)
    tr = A @ beta
    r = y - tr
    # annual cycle: sin/cos with 12-month period on month index
    S = np.vstack([np.sin(2*np.pi*t/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*t/12)]).T
    g, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(S, r, rcond=None)
    seas = S @ g
    rem = y - seas
    sm = gaussian_smooth(rem)
    mu, sd = sm.mean(), sm.std()
    prep[:, j] = (sm - mu) / sd
    params[b] = dict(mu=mu, sd=sd, g=g, beta=beta)

# --- blocks: m matching months, n=1 forward
m, n = 3, 1
nb = T - m - n + 1  # 6
blocks = [prep[i:i+m] for i in range(nb)]        # matching parts
fwd = [prep[i+m] for i in range(nb)]             # first forward month (prepared)
target_win = prep[T-m:T]                          # most recent m months

yv = target_win.flatten()
def mse(idx):
    B = np.hstack([blocks[i] for i in idx]).reshape(m*len(bands), len(idx), order='F')
    # solve nonneg least squares weights
    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    A = np.column_stack([blocks[i].flatten() for i in idx])
    wts, _ = nnls(A, yv)
    if wts.sum() < 1e-12: wts = np.ones(len(idx))/len(idx)
    else: wts = wts / wts.sum()
    err = np.mean((A @ wts - yv)**2)
    return err, wts

# stepwise selection
sel = [int(np.argmin([mse([i])[0] for i in range(nb)]))]
best, wts = mse(sel)
tol = 1e-4
while len(sel) < nb:
    cands = [i for i in range(nb) if i not in sel]
    errs = [(mse(sel+[i])[0], i) for i in cands]
    e, i = min(errs)
    if best - e > tol:
        sel.append(i); best, wts = mse(sel)
    else:
        break

# --- prediction in prepared space, then invert
pred_prep = sum(w * fwd[i] for w, i in zip(wts, sel))
tt = T + 1
S_t = np.array([np.sin(2*np.pi*tt/12), np.cos(2*np.pi*tt/12)])
out = {}
for j, b in enumerate(bands):
    p = params[b]
    val = pred_prep[j] * p["sd"] + p["mu"] + S_t @ p["g"]
    out[b] = float(val)
    print(f"{b} {val:.6f}")
print("selected blocks:", sel, "weights:", np.round(wts,4), "match mse:", best)
import json
json.dump({"prediction": out, "rationale": "Synthetic historical control: per band, annual sin/cos seasonal term (estimated after removing a linear trend) removed, remainder smoothed with a local-linear Gaussian kernel (bw=1.5) and standardized; bands stacked. Overlapping 3-month matching blocks with 1-month forward parts (6 blocks) are weighted by nonnegative least squares (normalized to sum 1) to reproduce the most recent 3 months across all bands jointly; blocks added stepwise while matching MSE falls by >1e-4. Prediction is the weighted combination of the blocks' first forward months in prepared space, then un-standardized with the target month's seasonal term added back."}, open("answer.json","w"), indent=1)
EOF
python predict.py
```

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

# Implement and run the synthetic historical control

The parcel's past is its comparison: blocks of its own earlier months are weighted to
reproduce its most recent months, and what followed those blocks becomes the forecast.
`references/method.md` describes the construction; every setting and every choice in it
is yours, made inside your program.

## Workflow

1. `python scripts/show_data.py` — the nine months, every band. The same data is in
   `data.csv` in this directory: one row per band per month, columns `band`, `period_id`
   (P01–P09 in time order), `month` (YYYY-MM), `mean_value`.
2. Read `references/method.md`. Decide how to build the blocks, what to match, how to fit
   and constrain the weights, how to select blocks, and how to form the prediction.
3. Write `predict.py`. It reads `data.csv` and prints one line per band, `BAND VALUE`, the
   predicted mean value for the next month. numpy, scipy and pandas are available; nothing
   outside this directory is, and there is no network.

steps.output:
# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, itertools, json

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
T = 9
X = np.zeros((len(bands), T))
for i,b in enumerate(bands):
    for j,p in enumerate([f'P{k:02d}' for k in range(1,10)]):
        X[i,j] = df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)].mean_value.iloc[0]

# standardize each band
Z = (X - X.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)) / X.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)

m, n = 3, 1
nb = T - m - n + 1  # 6 blocks
blocks = [list(range(s, s+m)) for s in range(nb)]
fwd = [s+m for s in range(nb)]
target = list(range(T-m, T))

# design matrix: rows = (band, month in window), cols = blocks
A = np.zeros((len(bands)*m, nb))
y = np.zeros(len(bands)*m)
for k,b in enumerate(blocks):
    for i in range(len(bands)):
        for t in range(m):
            A[i*m+t, k] = Z[i, b[t]]
            y[i*m+t] = Z[i, target[t]]

def fit(cols):
    Aa = A[:, cols]
    # nonnegative least squares via scipy
    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    w, r = nnls(Aa, y)
    return w, r

best = None
for r in range(1, nb+1):
    for cols in itertools.combinations(range(nb), r):
        w, res = fit(list(cols))
        mse = (res**2)/len(y)
        if best is None or mse < best[0]:
            best = (mse, cols, w)

mse, cols, w = best
print('kept blocks (start idx):', cols, 'weights:', np.round(w,3), 'mse:', mse)

# prediction: weighted combination of forward months (first forward month), in original space
pred = {}
for i,b in enumerate(bands):
    val = sum(wi * X[i, fwd[c]] for wi, c in zip(w, cols)) / w.sum()
    pred[b] = val
    print(b, val)

json.dump({'prediction': pred,
 'rationale': 'Synthetic historical control: standardized band series stacked; overlapping 3-month blocks with 1 forward month; nonnegative least-squares weights fitted to reproduce the last 3 months (P07-P09) across all bands jointly; best subset chosen exhaustively by matching MSE; prediction is the weighted combination of the blocks\' following months.'},
 open('answer.json','w'), indent=1)

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

"""Synthetic historical control: predict P10 band means from P01-P09 only."""
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, itertools
from scipy.optimize import nnls

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
bands = sorted(df.band.unique())
w = df.pivot(index="period_id", columns="band", values="mean_value").sort_index()
Y = w[bands].to_numpy()          # 9 x 8, P01..P09
T, B = Y.shape
m, n = 3, 1                       # matching length, forward length
nb = T - m - n + 1                # number of blocks (6)

# Preparation: standardize each band over P01-P09 (matching on observed scale
# after per-band standardization so bands contribute comparably, jointly).
mu, sd = Y.mean(0), Y.std(0)
Z = (Y - mu) / sd

target = Z[T-m:, :]               # matching window: most recent m months
blocks = [Z[i:i+m, :] for i in range(nb)]        # matching parts
fwd    = [Z[i+m:i+m+n, 0] if False else Y[i+m, :] for i in range(nb)]  # first forward month, observed

def mse(idx):
    A = np.hstack([blocks[i].ravel() for i in idx]).reshape(len(idx)*m, B)
    x, _ = nnls(A, target.ravel())
    if x.sum() <= 0: return np.inf, None
    x = x / x.sum()
    r = A @ x - target.ravel()
    return float(r @ r), x

# Exhaustive subset selection, lowest matching error wins
best = (np.inf, None, None)
for k in range(1, nb+1):
    for idx in itertools.combinations(range(nb), k):
        e, x = mse(idx)
        if e < best[0]:
            best = (e, idx, x)
e, idx, x = best
pred = sum(wt * fwd[i] for wt, i in zip(x, idx))
print("kept blocks (start month idx):", idx, "weights:", np.round(x,3), "match mse:", e)
for b, v in zip(bands, pred):
    print(b, round(float(v), 4))
EOF
python predict.py
```

import pandas as pd
import json

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('parcel.csv')
df = df.sort_values('month')
print(df)

# Synthetic historical control: for each band, predict next month as
# last observed value plus mean of historical month-over-month changes
bands = [c for c in df.columns if c not in ('month', 'parcel_id')]
pred = {}
for b in bands:
    series = df[b].values
    last = series[-1]
    diffs = np.diff(series)
    pred[b] = last + diffs.mean()
print(pred)
with open('answer.json','w') as f:
    json.dump(pred, f)

# Synthetic historical control for one parcel

The parcel's own past is its comparison. Nothing from any other parcel is used.

## Historical blocks
From the nine observed months P01–P09, form overlapping blocks. A block is m consecutive
months (its matching part) followed by the n months that came after it (its forward part).
Blocks slide one month at a time, so there are 9 − m − n + 1 of them; the last block's
forward part ends at P09. The matching window is the parcel's most recent m months.

## What is matched
Each band's nine months can be matched as observed, or after preparation: an annual sine
and cosine term is estimated for the band (after partialling out a low-order time trend in
the month index) and removed, the remainder is smoothed along time with a local-linear
Gaussian kernel of a chosen bandwidth, and the smoothed series is standardized to mean 0
and standard deviation 1 over P01–P09. Bands are stacked, so one set of block weights
serves every band.

## Weights and selection
Weights over the blocks are fitted so the weighted combination of the blocks' matching
parts reproduces the matching window, across all bands jointly, minimizing mean squared
error. A selection rule decides which blocks carry weight: stepwise (keep the single
best-fitting block, then add one block at a time while the error falls by more than a
tolerance) or exhaustive (every non-empty subset, lowest error wins).

## Prediction
The next month is predicted as the same weighted combination of what followed each kept
block — its first forward month, as observed — or, when the fit was made on the prepared
series, in the prepared space with the standardization undone and the target month's
seasonal term added back.

## What the fit can and cannot see
The fit sees P01–P09 only. The month to predict, P10 (2024-08), is withheld: no script
can read it and no setting may refer to it. The matching error reported by the fitter is
the error on the matching window inside P01–P09, not the error on P10.

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, itertools, json

df = pd.read_csv('data.csv')
bands = sorted(df['band'].unique())
periods = [f'P{i:02d}' for i in range(1,10)]
# matrix T x B
Y = np.array([[df[(df.band==b)&(df.period_id==p)]['mean_value'].iloc[0] for b in bands] for p in periods])

m, n = 3, 1
nb = 9 - m - n + 1  # number of blocks
# block i: matching part = Y[i:i+m], forward part = Y[i+m:i+m+n]
M = np.array([Y[i:i+m].ravel() for i in range(nb)])   # blocks x (m*B)
F = np.array([Y[i+m] for i in range(nb)])             # blocks x B (first forward month)
target = Y[9-m:].ravel()                              # matching window (last m months)

def fit(idx):
    A = M[list(idx)].T  # (m*B) x k
    # nonnegative least squares via scipy
    from scipy.optimize import nnls
    w, _ = nnls(A, target)
    pred = w @ F[list(idx)]
    err = np.mean((A @ w - target)**2)
    return err, w, pred

best = None
for k in range(1, nb+1):
    for idx in itertools.combinations(range(nb), k):
        err, w, pred = fit(idx)
        if best is None or err < best[0]:
            best = (err, idx, w, pred)
